model.rationale: The seat's deep Republican lean, Jackson's overwhelming fundraising edge, and near-certain pricing on prediction markets all point to an easy incumbent win, with no evidence suggesting a competitive race.

overview:
TX-13 is one of the most Republican-leaning House districts in the country, and Ronny Jackson returns as the incumbent with a dominant financial position. He has raised over $4 million and holds more than $5.4 million on hand, while Democrat Mark Nair has raised about $132,000 with under $15,000 available. Outside groups have added modest support behind Jackson, and no spending has targeted him.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the picture rests on district fundamentals and money. Prediction markets price Jackson's chances at roughly 97-98 percent, consistent with a seat that favored Republicans by about 23 points in recent partisan baselines. Absent an extraordinary development, the Republican incumbent is positioned to win another term by a wide margin.
